title: Denial-of-service attacks
starter: An online shop is unreachable for a whole Saturday. List everything that costs the company while the site is down.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Denial of service
facts: A denial-of-service (DoS) attack floods a server with requests so it can't respond to real users.
Nothing is stolen: the aim is disruption.
The service slows down or goes offline completely.
stations.challenge: What does a DoS attack set out to achieve?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A denial-of-service (DoS) attack floods a server with requests so it can't respond to real users.
Also credit: Nothing is stolen: the aim is disruption.

questions.q: What does a denial-of-service attack set out to do?
questions.a: Stop real users from being able to use a service

questions.q: What is the main cost of a DoS attack to a business?
questions.a: Downtime: lost sales and customers while the service is unavailable

stations.name: DDoS and botnets
facts: A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack uses many computers at once.
Infected computers under an attacker's control are called zombies, and the network of them is a botnet.
The owners usually have no idea their device is taking part.
stations.challenge: Why is a DDoS attack harder to block than a DoS attack?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack uses many computers at once.
Also credit: Infected computers under an attacker's control are called zombies, and the network of them is a botnet.

questions.a: A network of infected computers controlled by an attacker

questions.q: Why is a distributed attack harder to stop?
questions.a: The traffic comes from thousands of different addresses, so it's hard to tell it from real users

stations.name: 21 October 2016
facts: A huge DDoS attack hit Dyn, a company that runs DNS servers for much of the internet.
Netflix, Twitter, Spotify, Reddit, PayPal and many news sites became unreachable.
The Mirai botnet was made of hacked smart devices, such as cameras and routers, using default passwords.
stations.challenge: Why did taking down one company affect so many websites?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A huge DDoS attack hit Dyn, a company that runs DNS servers for much of the internet.
Also credit: Netflix, Twitter, Spotify, Reddit, PayPal and many news sites became unreachable.

questions.q: What were most of the devices in the Mirai botnet?
questions.a: Internet-connected devices such as cameras and routers, still using default passwords

questions.q: Why did attacking a DNS provider knock out so many sites?
questions.a: Without DNS, browsers couldn't turn domain names into IP addresses

stations.name: Effects
facts: Customers can't reach the service, so sales and trust are lost.
Staff can't work if internal systems are affected.
Sometimes a DDoS is a smokescreen while another attack happens elsewhere.
stations.challenge: List three effects of a week-long DDoS attack on an online shop.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Customers can't reach the service, so sales and trust are lost.
Also credit: Staff can't work if internal systems are affected.

questions.q: Which are effects of a successful DDoS attack on a company? Select all that apply.
questions.a: Customers can't buy anything while the site is down; Damage to the company's reputation; Staff unable to use internal systems

questions.q: Why might attackers launch a DDoS as a distraction?
questions.a: The security team is busy, so another attack may go unnoticed

stations.name: Defending the server
facts: Firewalls and filters can block suspicious traffic patterns.
Rate limiting caps how many requests one source can make.
Extra capacity and traffic-spreading services absorb large floods.
Intrusion detection systems and monitoring spot attacks early.
stations.challenge: Which defence would you buy first for a small online shop, and why?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Firewalls and filters can block suspicious traffic patterns.
Also credit: Rate limiting caps how many requests one source can make.

questions.q: How does rate limiting help against a DoS attack?
questions.a: It caps how many requests each source can make, so floods are throttled

questions.q: Which helps stop your devices being used in a botnet?
questions.a: Changing default passwords and keeping devices updated

stations.name: Watching the attacks
facts: Attack maps show DDoS traffic around the world in near real time.
Monitoring normal traffic makes unusual spikes obvious.
Many attacks are bought as a service for a few pounds, which is illegal.
stations.challenge: Discuss what the digital attack map shows and what patterns you notice.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Attack maps show DDoS traffic around the world in near real time.
Also credit: Monitoring normal traffic makes unusual spikes obvious.

questions.q: Why does knowing normal traffic patterns help?
questions.a: Because an unusual spike stands out as a possible attack

questions.q: Paying a website to 'stress test' someone else's server is:
questions.a: Illegal under the Computer Misuse Act

final.name: Final challenge: the anatomy of a DDoS

questions.q: Put the stages of a DDoS attack in order.
questions.a: Malware infects thousands of poorly secured devices → The infected devices become zombies in a botnet → The attacker sends a command to the botnet → Every zombie sends requests to the target server at once → The server runs out of capacity and stops responding to real users

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: Describe what a denial-of-service attack does to a service.
points: A denial-of-service (DoS) attack floods a server with requests so it can't respond to real users.
A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack uses many computers at once.
The service slows down or goes offline completely.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
